analysis:
Examined the complete patch and BASE/HEAD of scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py. The tests replace arbitrary-ref, credential-free ad-hoc building and master-only credentialed publication assertions (BASE 31–100) with a dev-push reusable-workflow contract. HEAD 120–140 pins the local workflow call, dev input, inherited secrets and permissions; 179–198 checks environment-guarded secret expressions and confines Apple secret references to the signing job; 200–220 checks Developer ID signing, notarization, fan-helper identity verification and publication serialization. These are static text assertions, not evidence that execution or deployment satisfies those contracts. No independently supported vulnerability is established in this test-only source scope.

Integration must inspect .github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml, release-provider.yml and release-swift.yml to verify the newly credentialed dev source path: checkout provenance, execution of branch-controlled build/publication code with Apple credentials, inherited-secret exposure, environment resolution and actual artifact version stamping (HEAD 150–151 only asserts the run-name marker). Compare the removed master-only publication boundary with the actual workflow changes rather than assuming dev has weaker branch protections. Relevant contracts are A-005/A-011 release authority, A-017 and T-054 independent artifact qualification, T-013/T-034 code identity, and TB-010/T-045 privileged helper integrity. Signing a dev artifact alone does not establish production serving authorization. The supplied tests do not change encryption, cache isolation (T-041), request authorization, billing or runtime admission; their implementations were not supplied. Deeper review is needed to resolve the release-workflow interactions, not because missing source proves a regression.
